Our own scene.

lines.text: Two years have gone by since you came to the farm. Early on this spring morning, someone slides the door open.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Morning! I hope I'm not too early. The whole village has been talking, so I came to tell you myself.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Every New Year we write in the village record who did what. This year there's a page just for you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Here, read it. Slowly, now. My handwriting isn't what it was.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: A traveler's page, for now. But the field remembers every row you dug. There's always next year.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: A new hand on the farm, it says. Two years ago that field was all weeds. Don't let anyone tell you that's small.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Village farmer. That's what we call someone we can't picture the village without anymore.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Keeper of the satoyama! The hills, the paddies, the people... you've looked after all of it.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Heart of the village. I've written a lot of pages in that book, and I've never written that one before.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: And between us, the old woman you stop to chat with every day thinks you're the best thing to happen here in years.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Grandma Tome said I could come too! Two years, huh? You're not the new one anymore.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: ...I'm still faster than you, though. Race you to the pond later?

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: I closed the store for an hour. Don't tell anyone.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: I only wanted to say the shelves have never been as busy as since you came. Thank you, really.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Hm. Came to see your face when you read it. That's all.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Good work, farmer. Bring me that hoe when it's dull. I'll make it sing.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: I walked all the way down from Sakurazaka with a flask of tea. It's still warm, I wrapped it twice.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Two years of you on my road. The cherries wouldn't know what to do without you now. Neither would I.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...Fumi said I should come. Said I should say something.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: So. Good work. Your stove's charcoal is on me, as long as I'm burning.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Climbed down with a bag of seed rice. Two years of you, and the terraces look younger for it.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: My wife would have liked you. She tasted everyone's water, you know. Yours is sweet. Good rice follows.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I ran the whole lane down! Here. New sandals, a tight pair and a loose pair. Two years' walking wore out your last ones.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I nearly left Kaminoda once, you know. I'm glad I'm still here to see this page. Wear them up the hill sometime.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: I ran up from the river with my boots still wet. Here. The first fish of the year, for the page. Grill it with salt, nothing else.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Two years ago you couldn't tell a chub from a dace. Now Hachiro asks you where they're biting. Don't let it go to your head.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: I brought the year's first fortune down from the shrine. Unopened. It's for your page, so you open it.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Two years of you walking up the shrine path. I've prayed for this village a long time. You're the first answer I can point to.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: I dyed a cloth for the record's cover. Indigo, twenty dips. It'll outlast the paper.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: When I came home I thought I'd failed in the city. Then you came, and kept at it for two years. That helped more than you know.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Nana made me wear my good jacket. She says a page in the village record deserves it, and she's right.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Two years ago that farm was stones and stubbornness. Now Sayo asks me why your greens sell first. I tell her: soil talks, and you listened.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Well! The record is written, but the seasons don't stop for it. Spring is waiting for you out there.
